Statistical Machine Learning Model for Stochastic
Optimal Planning of Distribution Networks
Considering a Dynamic Correlation
and Dimension Reduction
Xueqian Fu , Member, IEEE, Qinglai Guo , Senior Member, IEEE, and Hongbin Sun , Fellow, IEEE
Abstract—Distributed generation and reactive power resource
allocation will affect the economy and security of distribu-
tion networks. Deterministic scenario planning cannot solve the
problem of network uncertainties, which are introduced by
intermittent renewable generators and a variable demand for
electricity. However, stochastic programming becomes a problem
of great complexity when there is a large number of scenar-
ios to be analyzed and when the computational burden has an
adverse effect on the programming solution. In this paper, statis-
tical machine learning theories are proposed to quickly solve the
optimal planning for capacitors. Various technologies are used:
Markov chains and copula functions are formulated to capture
the variability and correlation of weather; consumption behav-
ior probability is involved in the weather-sensitive load model;
nearest neighbor theory and nonnegative matrix decomposition
are combined to reduce the dimensions and scenario scale of
stochastic variables; the stochastic response surface is used to
calculate the probabilistic power ﬂow; and probabilistic inequal-
ity theory is introduced to directly estimate the objective and
constraint functions of the stochastic programming model. The
effectiveness and efﬁciency of the proposed method are veriﬁed
by comparing the method with the scenario reduction algorithm
and the Monte Carlo method in a 33-bus distribution system.
Index Terms —Photovoltaic, capacitor, power grid planning,
probabilistic power ﬂow, statistical machine learning.
I. I NTRODUCTION
P
OWER grid planning is an important part of power system
planning. Its purpose is to determine the optimal grid
structure for load growth during the planning period and
a power planning scheme that can meet the demand for
the economical and reliable transmission of electricity. In
recent years, because of the interconnections between new
energy sources, such as large-scale wind and solar energy, and
stochastic factors, such as energy storage and weather-sensitive

loads, a large amount of uncertainty and stochastic behav-
ior has emerged in power systems’ sources. Thus, stochastic
optimal planning has become an essential subject of research
in power systems. Stochastic programming methods should
be applied instead of deterministic models when the power
ﬂow in a power grid changes from deterministic power ﬂow to
probabilistic power ﬂow (PPF). This change greatly interferes
with the accuracy of the PPF, so it is necessary to improve
the stochastic optimal planning method of a power grid with
a high proportion of stochastic factors.
To more accurately study the inﬂuence of uncertainties
on power systems, Borkowska ﬁrst presented PPF theory in
1974 [1]. PPF uses statistical knowledge to describe the uncer-
tainty in system state variables; PPF calculation methods can
be divided into three categories: simulation methods, analytical
methods and approximation methods. Monte Carlo simulation
is a typical simulation method. Because its calculation accu-
racy depends on the sampling scale, it has the shortcomings
of requiring heavy calculations and being time-consuming.
However, its convergence and accuracy are not affected by the
scale and complexity of the power system. The Monte Carlo
method is usually used as the reference standard by which
to measure other PPF calculation methods. The Nataf trans-
form can solve the model problem of correlated nonnormal
distributions, and Latin hypercube sampling can improve the
efﬁciency of Monte Carlo sampling for PPF calculations [2].
Fu et al. used a copula function to simulate the correlation
between photovoltaic (PV) power and heating, ventilating,
and air-conditioning (HV AC) loads, and the inﬂuence of the
thermoelectric correlation on the PPF was analyzed in a real
41-bus distribution system in China [3]. The analytical method
mainly includes the convolution method, the point estimation
method (PEM) and the semi-invariant method. The convolu-
tion method obtains the probability density function of the
state variables via the convolution operation of the probability
density function of the input stochastic variables [4], but the
derivation of this method involves a great deal of mathematics.
The PEM method does not require knowledge of the probabil-
ity density function of the input stochastic variables and uses
a Gram-Charlier expansion to approximate the expected value,
variance and cumulative distribution of state variables [5]. The
semi-invariant method obtains semi-invariants of the state vari-
ables from semi-invariants of input variables through algebraic

operations [6] and requires linearization of the power ﬂow
equation. For the approximation method, an agent model can
replace the actual PPF; this model has a high calculation
accuracy and efﬁciency. In [7], the response surface is used
to represent the thermoelectric hybrid PPF calculation with
a good accuracy and efﬁciency. However, the response sur-
face method cannot guarantee convergence by approximating
the stochastic response of the structure with polynomials. The
stochastic response surface method (SRSM) overcomes this
disadvantage and shows good accuracy and a high efﬁciency
in PPF calculations [8]. In summary, the existing statistical-
based PPF calculation model can address multidimensional
stochastic variables, but the methods available for dealing
with high-dimensional stochastic variables are not sufﬁciently
mature. In addition, more research is needed on the ability to
generalize PPF calculations based on agent models.
Stochastic planning is an important issue in distribution
networks, as it is a matter of the utmost importance to
ensure the safe and economic operation of a power grid with
a high proportion of new energy sources. Research has been
conducted in this ﬁeld of inquiry. Fu et al. presented a distri-
bution network planning model based on chance-constrained
programming that realizes the coordinated planning of pho-
tovoltaic power generation and reactive power devices, and
considered the balance of power quality and network loss when
the grid is running [9]. Zhang et al. presented a linearized
approximation algorithm to solve the interval reactive power
optimization model, and the ﬁrst-order terms of the Taylor
expansions of the interval functions were utilized to approx-
imate the interval reactive power optimization model [10].
An interval sequential quadratic programming algorithm that
provided a new method for solving the interval dynamic
reactive power optimization model was presented in [11]. It
has a strong robustness and engineering application ability.
Dynamic travel behaviors and the charge state of electric vehi-
cles have a detrimental effect on the optimal solution for the
capacity and conﬁguration of electric vehicle charging stations.
Based on the statistics of plug-in electric vehicles, Yang et al.
used Markov chains and queuing theory [12] to present
an optimal planning sizing model of fast-charging stations.
Ehsan and Yang harnessed heuristic moment matching to char-
acterize the uncertainty of representative scenarios [13]; their
method can coordinately plan intermittent renewable genera-
tors. Optimal planning research has been conducted in the ﬁeld
of demand response: [14] emphasized that energy planning
in heating/cooling systems management can minimize costs
and improve reliability in smart microgrids. It is imperative
that we provide power from a neighboring feeder or a dis-
tributed generation when a fault occurs in a feeder, and service
restoration requirements should include optimal infrastructure
planning of active distribution networks [15]. Optimal plan-
ning of PV power has been reinforced by extensive research,
and both region-speciﬁc solar power and temperature should
be formulated for the optimal planning of PV generation in
low voltage microgrids [16]. Chronological time-period clus-
tering can be used to determine the capacity expansion plans
in electricity networks and can overcome the problem where
time period aggregation approaches fail to properly capture the
mid-term dynamics of intermittent renewable generators [17].
In summary, the impact of stochastic characteristics introduced
by intermittent renewable generators on power grid planning
has been taken into account; however, it is still necessary
to achieve a coordinated balance between speed and accu-
racy in stochastic optimization models with a large number of
scenarios.
The novel contributions of this paper can be summarized
as follows. 1) The copula function and Markov chain the-
ory are used to model weather factors, considering not only
cross-correlation but also state transition probabilities. The
accurate modeling of weather factors ensures the accuracy of
weather-sensitive load simulations and intermittent renewable
generators. 2) The accuracy of the correlation among sources
and loads is the basis for the accurate calculation of PPF. The
total correlation is proposed as a measure for evaluating the
correlation of more than two variables, and a Monte Carlo
method is used to address the fact that the total correlation of
multiple variables is difﬁcult to calculate. 3) Large scenario
datasets and a high-dimensional uncertainty make calculating
the PPF complex and time-consuming. To avoid these draw-
backs, a novel method based on the nearest neighbor approach
and nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) is proposed to
produce SRSM input variables with low dimensionality and
a small size; the proposed PPF fast calculation method has
a good efﬁciency and accuracy. 4) The Chebyshev inequality
probability bound is then introduced to directly apply the PPF
to the constraints of the stochastic optimal planning model,
which can be efﬁciently solved via the proposed PPF fast
calculation method.
The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. First,
the uncertainty model of the source and load is described.
Second, a fast calculation method is presented to solve the
PPF calculation problems. Third, a stochastic planning model
is presented to solve the optimal planning problems in distri-
bution networks. Finally, four cases are simulated to verify the
effectiveness of the proposed method.
II. G
LOBAL VIEW OF THE PROPOSED MODEL
Statistical machine learning has a unique deﬁnition, which
involves science about the probability and statistics model
based on data, and it is then used to predict and analyze
data. It is an interdisciplinary subject, involving probability
theory, statistics, approximation theory, convex analysis, algo-
rithm complex theory and other disciplines. Statistical machine
learning is not only the core issue in the ﬁeld of artiﬁcial
intelligence; it has also been one of the most active research
branches in the ﬁeld of smart grid in recent years.
The motivation in this paper is to improve the efﬁciency of
calculating PPF via statistical machine learning, which enables
further accelerating the solution of stochastic optimal planning
on distribution networks. This section focuses on a comprehen-
sive view of the statistical machine learning methodology by
highlighting the reasons and goals of addressing the problem
with stochastic optimal planning of distribution networks.
A method that integrates the statistical machine learning mod-
els is proposed in this paper, and it uses a set of submodel
methods as follows.

III. U
NCERTAINTY MODEL OF THE SOURCE AND LOAD
First, we give a concrete explanation on the dynamic corre-
lation. Second, we use the Markov chain and copula function

A. Dynamic Correlation
As shown in Fig. 1, both the HV AC load and PV power
can be affected by ﬂuctuating weather, so correlations exist
between them. The correlation between the HV AC load and
PV power was described in [3], and this paper considers differ-
ent degrees of correlation under different weather scenarios.
PV power is sensitive to solar radiation, and HV AC load is
sensitive to temperature. The correlation degree between solar
radiation and temperature is different under different weather
scenarios, so the correlation degree between the HV AC load
and PV power is also different under different weather sce-
narios. One can suppose that there is a type of correlation
in a weather scenario, so dynamic correlation is needed to
describe weather scenario changes. To describe the changing
law of weather scenarios, the dynamic correlation between
solar radiation and temperature will be modeled and further
elaborated on in the next section.

It should be noted that the Chebyshev inequality is used
for security constraints rather than the economy objective in
this paper. If the objective function is too conservative it
will reduce the economy performance, but this paper uses
the mathematical expectation to describe the objective; for
the safety constraints, if it meets the conservative condition
it must also meet the safety constraints under the worst con-
ditions. The conservative security constraints may reduce the
feasible solutions, but this does not directly lead to a decline
in the objective performance. Only when the eliminated fea-
sible solution region includes the optimal solution does the
objective performance decline.
The Chebyshev inequality is used in the stochastic optimal
planning model, but in principle the constraint derived by
the Chebyshev inequality is conservative. Monte Carlo can
compare the Chebyshev inequality to address this issue. The
Chebyshev inequality uses very little information, and only
a mathematical expectation and variance are involved. The
Chebyshev inequality tells us that the probability for a ran-
dom variable deviating from its mean value is limited by its
variance. When ε is smaller, the calculation results are more
accurate. The Chebyshev inequality cannot be wrong; at most
it is conservative. Monte Carlo has a better accuracy than the
Chebyshev inequality, but the time cost of Monte Carlo is
greater than that of the Chebyshev inequality.

Statistical machine learning is a science concerned with
data-based probabilistic statistical models that are constructed
by computers and used to predict and analyze data. It is not
only the core problem in the ﬁeld of artiﬁcial intelligence but
it has also become one of the most active research branches
in the ﬁeld of electrical engineering. Intermittent renewable
generators and stochastic electricity use behaviors that clash
with distribution networks with complex randomicity, making
the stochastic programming model very difﬁcult to solve. In
light of the above stochastic programming problems, a novel
stochastic programming method is proposed based on statisti-
cal machine learning theories, including digital characteristics,
